item.title: Damaging Heavy Swell Alert issued for parts of Fiji
item.description: A Damaging Heavy Swell Alert is now in force for Southwest Viti Levu waters, the Yasawa and Mamanuca waters, Kadavu Passage, Koro Sea and Southern Lau waters. The Nadi Weather Office says a high-pressure system to the far southwest of Fiji is expected to generate and direct damaging heavy swells towards Fiji waters from later tomorrow.
item.content:encoded:
A Damaging Heavy Swell Alert is now in force for Southwest Viti Levu waters, the Yasawa and Mamanuca waters, Kadavu Passage, Koro Sea and Southern Lau waters.

The Nadi Weather Office says a high-pressure system to the far southwest of Fiji is expected to generate and direct damaging heavy swells towards Fiji waters from later tomorrow.

It says damaging southwesterly swells are expected to develop, with wave heights reaching up to four metres over open waters.

Wave periods of up to 16 seconds are also forecast from later Saturday.

People travelling by sea and those living or carrying out activities in affected coastal areas should remain alert to changing sea conditions.

item.title: Court to rule this afternoon on FICAC disclosure issue in Prof. Prasad's FICAC case
item.description: Naidu further told the court that it now appeared other statements may also exist and questioned what other potentially relevant material could be contained in the closed FEP 41/24 file. He says the issue is therefore no longer limited to the two statements because the defence does not know what other material may exist that could be relevant or assist Prasad's defence.
item.content:encoded:
Naidu further told the court that it now appeared other statements may also exist and questioned what other potentially relevant material could be contained in the closed FEP 41/24 file.

He says the issue is therefore no longer limited to the two statements because the defence does not know what other material may exist that could be relevant or assist Prasad's defence.

Naidu says the matter raises broader questions about FICAC's handling of potentially relevant evidence and its disclosure obligations.

He submitted that a prosecutor has a duty to the court which overrides the prosecutor's interest in the case and also has a fundamental duty to disclose relevant material, including material that may assist an accused person.

Naidu says somebody within FICAC has to take responsibility for the prosecution's disclosure obligations and, if those obligations have been breached, it could have consequences for the entire trial.

He further submitted that if potentially helpful information was withheld internally because an investigator considered it unreliable or irrelevant, this raised concerns about FICAC's approach to material that could assist an accused person.

Naidu says the defence has been fundamentally disadvantaged regardless of where within FICAC responsibility for any non-disclosure may lie.

He says disclosure at this stage may not necessarily resolve the issue because the trial has already progressed on the basis of the material previously disclosed.

Naidu says pre-trial conferences had already taken place and facts and documents had been agreed on the basis of the disclosure available to the defence at the time.

He says the defence may have approached those matters differently if all relevant material had been disclosed earlier and its trial strategy may also have been affected.

item.title: Religious statues damaged during Nakasi temple break-in
item.description: Religious statues have been damaged in an act of sacrilege during a break-in at the Gopal Sadhu Hanuman Gadhi Mandir in Nakasi. Temple Treasurer Ashish Prasad told fijivillage News that the incident occurred between 1am and 2am.
item.content:encoded:
Religious statues have been damaged in an act of sacrilege during a break-in at the Gopal Sadhu Hanuman Gadhi Mandir in Nakasi.

Temple Treasurer Ashish Prasad told fijivillage News that the incident occurred between 1am and 2am.

A video sent to fijivillage shows items inside the temple scattered in search for valuables and cash.

Prasad is calling for strict action against those responsible.

The matter has been reported to Police, who have visited the scene.

item.title: Enforcement alone will not solve Fiji’s drug problem - Kamikamica
item.description: Fiji needs a broader response to the growing challenge of illicit drugs, with greater focus on why young people are becoming vulnerable to drug use. Speaking at the launch of Christian youth radio station Life FM at Studio 6 this morning , Acting Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development Manoa Kamikamica says enforcement alone will not solve the problem.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji needs a broader response to the growing challenge of illicit drugs, with greater focus on why young people are becoming vulnerable to drug use.

Speaking at the launch of Christian youth radio station Life FM at Studio 6 this morning , Acting Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development Manoa Kamikamica says enforcement alone will not solve the problem.

He says while law enforcement agencies must continue working to disrupt those who traffic and profit from illicit drugs, Fiji must also understand the factors that are making young people vulnerable.

Kamikamica says questions need to be asked about whether young people feel connected to their families and communities, whether they have opportunities and hope, and whether they have positive role models and somewhere to turn when they are struggling.

He says the response must involve families, schools, communities, health professionals, civil society, faith organisations, the private sector and the media.

Kamikamica says Fiji must be prepared to not only say no to drugs, but also say yes to purpose, opportunity, belonging and hope.

He says the same principle applies to other challenges in communities, including HIV and broader public health concerns.

Kamikamica says these difficult issues cannot be addressed through silence and require accurate information, responsible behaviour, prevention, access to health services and compassion.

He says stigma should never prevent a person from seeking help.

Kamikamica says a mature society is one that can confront difficult realities honestly while retaining its humanity.

He says responsible media organisations also have an important role in starting conversations that need to be started.

Kamikamica says Life FM can encourage young people to make responsible choices, provide information, give families a reason to talk and challenge harmful behaviours, while reminding people who are struggling that they should not be abandoned.

Meanwhile, Life FM operates under United Christian Broadcasters International Ltd, and is part of a Christian media movement operating in more than 30 countries across the Asia-Pacific region.
